questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A fumigation company was hired to eliminate pests in one of two buildings in a condominium complex that shared a common wall. The owners of the complex told the fumigation company that the common wall separating the infested building from the uninfested building was an impenetrable fire wall. The fumigation company did its own thorough inspection and determined that the buildings were indeed completely separated by the wall. Residents of the condominium units in the building that was to be sprayed were told to evacuate, but the residents of the uninfested building were told that they could remain while the other building was treated.
During and shortly after the fumigation, in which a highly toxic chemical was used, many residents of the uninfested building became sick. It was determined that their illnesses were caused by the fumigation chemical.
In fact, there was a hole in the fire wall separating the two buildings, but because it could only be observed from a specific position in the crawl space underneath the floor of the uninfested building, it had not been discovered by either the fumigation company or any previous building inspector.
Are the residents of the uninfested building likely to prevail in a tort action against the fumigation company?

choices.A: No, because the condominium complex owners were responsible for accurately conveying the condition of their buildings.
choices.B: No, because the fumigation company exercised a high level of care.
choices.C: Yes, because the fumigation company can be held strictly liable for its activity.
choices.D: Yes, because the fumigation company put a dangerous product into the stream of commerce.

questions.explanation:
Abnormally dangerous activity

An activity is abnormally dangerous when:

  • it is uncommon in the community and
  • it presents a foreseeable & highly significant risk of physical harm that cannot be mitigated by reasonable care

A defendant is strictly liable (liable regardless of fault) for the plaintiff's harm caused by an abnormally dangerous activity. An activity is abnormally dangerous when it (1) is uncommon in the community and (2) creates a foreseeable and highly significant risk of physical harm to the plaintiff that cannot be mitigated by reasonable care.

Here, the use of highly toxic chemicals to fumigate a building (uncommon activity in the community) is an abnormally dangerous activity since it is highly probable that persons exposed to the chemicals will become sick (foreseeable and significant risk of harm). And since several residents became sick after their exposure to the chemicals, the fumigation company will likely be strictly liable for their harm.

(Choice A) The significant risk of harm posed by an abnormally dangerous activity cannot be mitigated by anyone's use of reasonable care. Therefore, the condominium owners' failure to exercise reasonable care (by not accurately conveying the condition of their buildings) will not extinguish the fumigation company's strict liability.

(Choice B) A defendant engaged in an abnormally dangerous activity is strictly liable for the plaintiff's harm regardless of the level of care used in carrying out the activity. Therefore, the fumigation company's exercise of a high level of care does not negate its strict liability to the sick residents.

(Choice C) A defendant engaged in an abnormally dangerous activity is strictly liable for the plaintiff's harm regardless of the level of care used in carrying out the activity. Therefore, the fumigation company's exercise of a high level of care does not negate its strict liability to the sick residents.

(Choice D) A defendant may be strictly liable for distributing a defective or dangerous product into the stream of commerce, but that is irrelevant here since the fumigation company provided a service—not a product.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant is strictly liable for harm caused by an abnormally dangerous activity—an uncommon activity that poses a foreseeable and highly significant risk of physical harm that cannot be mitigated by reasonable care. Therefore, the use of reasonable care is no defense.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 20 (Am. Law Inst. 2010) (abnormally dangerous activity).
  • Old Island Fumigation, Inc. v. Barbee, 604 So. 2d 1246 (Fla. Dist. Ct. App. 1992).
questions.zh-question:
一家熏蒸公司受雇为一栋公寓大楼中的两栋建筑之一进行害虫消杀，这两栋建筑共用一堵墙。大楼业主告诉熏蒸公司，隔开受虫害侵扰和未受侵扰建筑的共用墙是一堵无法穿透的防火墙。熏蒸公司自己进行了彻底检查，并确定这两栋建筑确实被这堵墙完全隔开。需要喷洒药剂的公寓单位住户被告知需要撤离，但未受侵扰大楼的住户被告知，在另一栋建筑进行处理期间，他们可以留下。

在熏蒸期间和之后不久，由于使用了剧毒化学品，许多未受侵扰大楼的住户生病了。经确定，他们的疾病是由熏蒸化学品引起的。

事实上，隔开两栋建筑的防火墙上有一个洞，但由于只能从未受侵扰建筑地板下的狭小空隙中的特定位置才能观察到，因此熏蒸公司或之前的任何建筑检查员都未能发现。

在针对熏蒸公司的侵权诉讼中，未受侵扰大楼的住户是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为公寓大楼的业主有责任准确传达其建筑物的状况。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为熏蒸公司已尽到高度的注意义务。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为熏蒸公司应对其活动承担严格责任。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为熏蒸公司将危险产品投入了商业流通过程。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Strict Liability and Products Liability - Abnormally dangerous activities

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：异常危险活动（abnormally dangerous activity）一旦成立，做事再小心也还是要担严格责任。

三秒认题路径：

高毒化学 → 非常见活动 → 高风险不可防 → 严格责任 → 选 C

核心法律规则

异常危险活动（abnormally dangerous activity）的考场意思：这类活动本身就太危险，不看你有没有过失。只要活动在社区里不常见，而且会带来可预见的、很高的身体伤害风险，且这种风险不能靠合理注意避免，行为人就可能要承担严格责任（strict liability）。

对这题来说，熏蒸（fumigation）时使用高毒化学物质，正好落在这个框里。重点不是公司有没有尽到注意义务，而是它做的是不是这种“天生危险”的事。

核心判例：Old Island Fumigation, Inc. v. Barbee — 说明高毒熏蒸可构成异常危险活动，过失谨慎不能把严格责任洗掉。

思维导图

先看：这题是不是在问“能不能因为做了高危活动而直接担责”？
事实触发：高毒化学、住户因暴露后生病、活动在社区里不常见。
规则门槛 1：是不是 异常危险活动（abnormally dangerous activity）？
如果 YES：进入严格责任，不再靠“我已经很小心”脱身。
如果 NO：才回到普通过失分析。
规则门槛 2：失分点：合理注意（reasonable care）不能切断严格责任
公司自己做了仔细检查，最多说明它没过失；但严格责任看的是活动属性，不看小心程度。
结论：居民因毒化学受害 → 直接打到严格责任 → 选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：公司已经自己检查过、还让另一栋楼留在原地，听起来很谨慎，所以不该赔。

但考试真正问的是：这是不是 异常危险活动（abnormally dangerous activity）。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

换句话说，合理注意只能救过失题，救不了严格责任题；而且 fire wall 有没有漏洞，不会改变“高毒熏蒸本身就危险”这个主线。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的 highly toxic chemical 熏蒸属于异常危险活动，受害住户已因暴露生病，所以公司要按活动本身承担严格责任。

❌ 事实误判 | 责任转移偷换

✕ A: 把 owners 的失误当成免责理由，但严格责任不会被别人说错话冲掉。

❌ 法律适用 | 过失标准误套

✕ B: 你被 high level of care 骗了；这里不是比谁更小心，而是看活动本身是否危险。

❌ 概念混淆 | 产品责任混用

✕ D: 把 stream of commerce 硬塞进来，但本题是服务型熏蒸，不是产品投放。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是过失题还是严格责任题；只要锁定异常危险活动，就别再用“我很小心”去找出路。

考场速记

记住一句：异常危险活动（abnormally dangerous activity）一旦成立，reasonable care 不是抗辩。

这类题先抓“活动本身危险不危险”，再看“是否社区少见 + 风险高且不可靠注意消掉”。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A retired man who had been a sales representative for a drill manufacturer listed a few of his tools manufactured by his former employer on an online garage-sale website. A woman purchased one of the man's listed power drills to use in her home-remodeling business. The power drill had never been used and was still sealed in its original box. The drill manufacturer had used all available techniques to inspect the drill for defects. The drill manufacturer intended the power drill to be used on wood only and therefore included on the drill's box a warning against using the drill on metal or masonry.
One week later, the woman was using the power drill to put holes in a brick wall when the drill bit flew off the drill due to a defective component and caused her to sustain a severe eye injury.
Traditional common-law rules regarding contributory negligence apply in this jurisdiction.
If the woman asserts a strict products liability claim against the man, is she likely to recover?

choices.A: No, because the man was not a commercial supplier.
choices.B: No, because the woman used the drill in an unintended manner.
choices.C: Yes, because the drill had a defective component part.
choices.D: Yes, because the man was a retailer of the power drill.

questions.explanation:
Products liability
Was plaintiff harmed by a product?
Yes
Who is the defendant?
Commercial seller
(eg, manufacturer,
distributor, retailer)
Causes of action
• Strict products liability (preferred)
• Negligence
• Misrepresentation
• Intentional tort
Noncommercial seller
(eg, garage sale)
Causes of action
• Negligence
• Misrepresentation
• Intentional tort
Service provider
(eg, doctor, dentist)
No products liability

Strict products liability applies to commercial suppliers—ie, persons in the business of manufacturing, distributing, or selling the type of defective product that caused the plaintiff harm. However, it does not apply to casual sellers—ie, persons conducting occasional sales outside their regular course of business.

Here, the man is a casual seller (not a commercial supplier) because he sold the power drill at an online garage sale—not in the regular course of business. Therefore, although the man sold the defective drill to the woman, he is not subject to strict products liability, and the woman is unlikely to recover.

(Choice B) Misuse is a defense to strict products liability when a product was used in an unintended, unforeseeable manner. Here, the woman used the drill in an unintended manner, despite the manufacturer's warning against using the drill on masonry (ie, brick). But that warning shows that her misuse was foreseeable.

(Choice C) It is irrelevant in this case that the drill had a defective component part. The man is only a casual seller, so he cannot be held strictly liable for the defective drill.

(Choice D) Any commercial supplier along the chain of distribution—including retailers—may be subject to strict products liability if the product contained a defect when it left the supplier's control. While the man likely would have been considered a retailer in his former job, he is only a casual seller in this case.

📌 Educational Objective

Strict products liability is only imposed on commercial suppliers (persons who manufacture, distribute, or sell products as part of their business)—not casual sellers (persons conducting occasional sales outside their regular course of business).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Prods. Liab. § 1 cmt. c, § 20 (Am. Law Inst. 1998) (defining commercial supplier).
questions.zh-question:
主题：侵权法（Torts）— 严格责任（Strict Liability）与产品责任（Products Liability）

题目：
一名已退休男子曾担任某钻孔机制造商的销售代表，他在一家网络车库甩卖网站上列出了几件由其前雇主制造的工具。某女子从该男子列出的电钻中购买了一台，准备用于她的家装生意。该电钻从未使用过，仍封存在原包装盒内。电钻制造商已采用所有可用技术检查该电钻是否存在缺陷。该制造商原本意图该电钻仅用于木材，因此在电钻盒上附有警告，禁止将该电钻用于金属或 masonry（砌体/砖石）材料。

一周后，该女子在用这台电钻为砖墙钻孔时，由于某个有缺陷的部件，钻头从电钻上飞脱，导致她遭受严重眼部伤害。

本管辖区适用关于 contributory negligence（共同过失）的传统普通法规则。

如果该女子对该男子提出 strict products liability（严格产品责任）主张，她是否很可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为该男子不是商业供应商（commercial supplier）。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为该女子以非预期方式使用了该电钻。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为该电钻存在有缺陷的部件（defective component part）。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为该男子是该电钻的零售商（retailer）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Strict Liability and Products Liability - Strict products liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：严格产品责任（strict products liability）只打到商业供应者（commercial supplier），偶尔转卖的闲置卖家（casual seller）一般不背这个锅。

三秒认题路径：

卖家是谁 → 商业卖家吗 → 闲置转卖吗 → 只能一般侵权 → 选 No

核心法律规则

严格产品责任（strict products liability）只针对把这类产品当生意来做的人，考场意思：你得先看被告是不是在制造、分销、销售同类产品的商业供应者（commercial supplier）。偶尔卖旧物（casual seller）不是这个队伍里的人，考场意思：即使他卖出的东西真的有缺陷，也通常不能直接按严格责任打他。

这里的关键不是电钻后来怎么坏，而是男人只是把自己旧工具挂到网上卖，考场意思：这是garage sale式的零散转卖，不是常规经营。女人可以想别的理论，但这道题问的是严格产品责任，所以先卡在被告身份这一步。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts: Prods. Liab. § 1 cmt. c, § 20 — 说明严格产品责任只压在商业供应者身上，不压在偶发转卖者身上。

思维导图

先问：能不能把男人当成严格责任被告？
1.商业供应者（commercial supplier）？
不能。网上处理旧工具，只是偶发转卖，不是常规经营。
2.既然不是商业卖家，就不能走严格产品责任（strict products liability）。
3.后面的“电钻有缺陷 / 用错场景”都不是救命点。
缺陷再真，也要先有能背严格责任的卖家。
结论：对男人提严格产品责任，答案是 No。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：电钻真的有缺陷，而且女人还受了重伤，所以应该能赢。

但考试真正问的是：被告能不能先被放进严格产品责任（strict products liability）的名单里。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

另一个坑是把“男人以前做过销售”当成现在的商业身份；考场只看这次卖东西是不是在正常经营里，不看他职业史有多体面。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 online garage-sale 说明男人只是偶发转卖旧工具，不是 商业供应者（commercial supplier），所以不能对他主张严格产品责任。

❌ 法律适用 | 用错免责点

✕ B: 盯着 unintended manner，却忘了先看被告身份。

❌ 事实误判 | 夸大缺陷细节

✕ C: 把 defective component 当成足够理由，忽略男人不是可被严格追责的卖家。

❌ 概念混淆 | 旧职业当现身份

✕ D: 以前像 retailer，不等于这次转卖时还是商业零售商。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定被告身份，再看能不能进入严格责任；身份不过关，后面的缺陷和误用都先放一边。

考场速记

记住一句：严格产品责任（strict products liability）先问“谁在卖”，再问“货有没有坏”。

口诀：商业卖家才上桌，偶尔转卖先出局。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A construction worker was using a nail gun to reshingle the roof of a residence. While the construction worker was near the edge of the roof, a manufacturing defect in the gun caused a nail to be discharged from the gun at an angle rather than directly downward. A 10-year-old child, who was playing in the yard below, was struck by the nail and seriously injured. The child's parents, on behalf of their child, have brought a strict products liability action against the construction company that employed the construction worker. The construction company can establish that, although the child was not negligent, her parents were negligent in allowing her to play near the construction work occurring on the roof.
Can the construction company successfully defend against this action?

choices.A: No, because the construction company is vicariously liable for the construction worker's conduct.
choices.B: No, because the nail gun used by the construction worker had a manufacturing defect.
choices.C: Yes, because the nail gun was used to provide a service.
choices.D: Yes, because the parents' contributory negligence will be imputed to the child to reduce the construction company's damages.

questions.explanation:
Strict products liability actions can only be maintained against commercial sellers who are in the business of selling or otherwise distributing the type of defective product that harmed the plaintiff. As a result, someone who merely used a defective product to provide a service is not subject to strict products liability for any harm to persons or property caused by the defect.

Here, the child was injured because of a manufacturing defect in the nail gun. But since the construction worker—and vicariously the construction company—was using the nail gun to reshingle the roof, the defective product was merely used to provide a service. As a result, the construction company can successfully defend against this action for strict products liability.

(Choice A) Employers can be held vicariously liable for an employee's tortious conduct under the doctrine of respondeat superior. But here, the construction worker (employee) is not strictly liable for the child's injury caused by the defective nail gun because the worker was not a commercial seller of the nail gun. As a result, the construction company (employer) is also not strictly liable.

(Choice B) The nail gun did have a manufacturing defect, which could impose strict liability (ie, liability without proof of fault) on the manufacturer and other commercial sellers of the gun. But strict liability would not be imposed on someone who merely used the nail gun to provide a service (eg, reshingle a roof).

(Choice C) The nail gun was used to provide a service, and therefore the construction company is not subject to strict products liability for harm caused by the defect.

(Choice D) Under the rule of pure comparative negligence (default rule on the MBE), a plaintiff's contributory negligence reduces the plaintiff's recovery by his/her proportionate share of fault. However, a parent's negligence will not be imputed (ie, assigned) to a child-plaintiff in a suit against a third party. And even if it were, this would merely reduce the child's damages—not serve as a complete defense to strict products liability.

📌 Educational Objective

Someone who merely used a defective product to provide a service is not subject to strict products liability for harm to persons or property caused by the defect.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Prods. Liab. §§ 1, 20 (Am. Law Inst. 1998) (liability of commercial suppliers).

该司法管辖区遵循纯粹比较过失(pure comparative negligence)规则。

该建筑公司能否成功地对此诉讼进行抗辩？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为建筑公司对建筑工人的行为负有替代责任(vicariously liable)。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为建筑工人使用的钉枪存在制造缺陷。
zh-choices.C: 能，因为建筑公司可以因父母的共同过失(contributory negligence)而减少任何损害赔偿。
zh-choices.D: 能，因为建筑工人仅仅是使用钉枪来更换屋顶瓦片。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Strict Liability and Products Liability - Strict products liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：严格产品责任（strict products liability）只能找卖产品的人，单纯拿有缺陷的工具去提供服务的人，不会因为这个缺陷被追严格产品责任。

三秒认题路径：

缺陷工具 → 提供服务 → 不是卖家 → 不能追严格责任 → 选 C

核心法律规则

只抓这条规则就够了

严格产品责任（strict products liability）只打到把产品卖出去或分销出去的商业卖家；考场意思：你得是“卖产品的人”，不是“拿产品干活的人”。

如果只是把有缺陷的产品拿来提供服务，比如用钉枪（nail gun）帮屋主重新铺屋顶，责任通常不会落到这个服务提供者身上。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts: Prods. Liab. §§ 1, 20 — 只有商业分销者才是严格产品责任的靶子，单纯服务使用者不是。

思维导图

有缺陷钉枪 制造缺陷
→
施工工人 只是拿来干活
→
施工公司 服务使用者
→
不是商业卖家 不在责任靶心
→
结果 不能以严格产品责任告成

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然钉枪真的有manufacturing defect，那当然就能直接告施工公司。

但考试真正问的是：谁是把产品卖进市场的人，谁只是拿它来完成一项服务；后者不因为工具坏了就自动背严格产品责任。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的关键是钉枪只是被拿来重铺屋顶，施工公司是服务使用者，不是商业卖家，所以不能被追严格产品责任。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把雇主的普通代理责任混进严格产品责任了。

❌ 法律适用 | 缺陷对象误判

✕ B: 只盯着manufacturing defect，忘了被告不是卖家。

❌ 事实误判 | 代位过度延伸

✕ D: 亲属过失不会直接扣到孩子头上。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定被告身份，再问他是卖产品还是只是用产品做服务。

考场速记

记住一句话：严格产品责任（strict products liability）先找“卖家”，再看“缺陷”。只拿缺陷产品来提供服务的人，通常不进这个口袋。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A tire manufacturer sold 100 car tires to a retailer. The retailer sold four of these tires to a woman. The woman took the tires to her mechanic to install on her car, but the mechanic informed her that they were the wrong size. The woman immediately returned the tires to the retailer. The retailer examined the tires thoroughly and determined that they were in the same condition they had been in when they left the retailer's store. The retailer marked the tires "Not brand new" and discounted them by 15%. A landscaper bought the tires at the discounted price and had them installed on the truck he used to transport tools for his business.
Three days after the tires were installed and before the landscaper had driven the truck with the new tires, he discovered that all four tires had gone flat, causing him to miss two landscaping appointments scheduled that day. Upon investigation, it was revealed that the tires had been improperly tempered when they were manufactured. The landscaper sued the manufacturer based on a strict products liability theory to recover damages for his lost business.
Which of the following is the manufacturer's best defense?

choices.A: By paying the discounted price, the landscaper assumed the risk that the tires were not reasonably fit for the ordinary purposes for which they were being sold.
choices.B: The manufacturer is not liable for the landscaper's purely economic loss.
choices.C: The retailer's sale of the tires to the woman broke the chain of liability to the manufacturer.
choices.D: There were no implied warranties on the tires because they were labeled "Not brand new."

questions.explanation:
Elements of strict products liability
Δ was commercial seller
  • Manufacturer
  • Distributor
  • Retailer
+
Product defective at time
left Δ's control
  • Manufacturing defect
  • Design defect
  • Failure to warn
+
Defect caused π
physical harm
  • Bodily harm
  • Property damage
π = plaintiff; Δ = defendant

A strict products liability claim requires proof of the following elements:

  • The defendant was a commercial seller (e.g., manufacturer, as seen here).
  • The product was defective when it left the defendant's control.
  • The defect caused the plaintiff's physical harm (i.e., bodily harm or property damage).

As a result, claims for purely economic losses are not allowed. In products liability cases, purely economic losses include any harm to the defective product as well as consequential damages arising therefrom (e.g., lost profits).

Here, the landscaper purchased used tires from the retailer for his truck. Three days later, the tires went flat due to a manufacturing defect (i.e., the tires were improperly tempered). This caused the landscaper to lose wages after missing two landscaping appointments (purely economic loss). Therefore, the manufacturer's best defense to this strict products liability claim is that the manufacturer is not liable for the landscaper's purely economic loss.

(Choice B) The implied warranty of merchantability warrants that a product is generally acceptable and reasonably fit for the ordinary purposes for which it is being sold. Assumption of the risk is a defense to breach of this warranty. But here, the landscaper sued under a strict products liability theory, not for breach of an implied warranty.

(Choice C) The chain of liability was not broken when the retailer sold the tires to the woman. That is because the tires were defective when they left the manufacturer's control.

(Choice D) Labeling the tires "Not brand new" is insufficient to disclaim the implied warranties. Additionally, the landscaper sued under a strict products liability theory—not for breach of an implied warranty.

📌 Educational Objective

Strict products liability claims require proof of physical harm (i.e., bodily harm or property damage). Claims for purely economic loss, including harm to the defective product and consequential damages arising therefrom, are not allowed.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Prods. Liab. § 21 (Am. L. Inst. 1998) (explaining that a strict products liability action requires proof that the plaintiff suffered physical harm, which does not include pure economic loss).
questions.zh-question:
题目：侵权法（Torts）——严格责任（Strict Liability）与产品责任（Products Liability）

一家轮胎制造商向一家零售商出售了100条汽车轮胎。该零售商将其中四条轮胎卖给了一名女性。该女性把轮胎拿给她的机械师安装在她的汽车上，但机械师告诉她这些轮胎尺寸不对。该女性立即将轮胎退回给零售商。零售商仔细检查了轮胎，确认它们的状况与离开零售商店时相同。零售商在轮胎上标注“Not brand new”，并将价格下调15%。一名园林工（landscaper）以折扣价购买了这些轮胎，并将其安装在他用来运送其业务工具的卡车上。

轮胎安装三天后、且在园林工驾驶装有新轮胎的卡车之前，他发现四条轮胎全部都瘪了，导致他错过了当天安排的两次园林服务预约。经调查发现，这些轮胎在制造时被错误加热处理（improperly tempered）。园林工基于严格产品责任（strict products liability）理论起诉制造商，要求赔偿其业务损失。

以下哪一项是制造商最好的抗辩？

zh-choices.A: 园林工通过支付折扣价，承担了这些轮胎并不适合其通常销售用途（reasonably fit for the ordinary purposes for which they were being sold）的风险。
zh-choices.B: 制造商对园林工纯粹的经济损失（purely economic loss）不承担责任。
zh-choices.C: 零售商将轮胎卖给该女性这一行为切断了制造商的责任链（chain of liability）。
zh-choices.D: 由于轮胎标注为“Not brand new”，因此这些轮胎不存在默示担保（implied warranties）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Strict Liability and Products Liability - Products liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：严格产品责任（strict products liability）里，原告如果只想要丢失营业收入这类纯经济损失（purely economic loss），通常不能拿这个理论去告制造商。

三秒认题路径：

严格责任 → 看损害类型 → 只有经济损失 → 不能立案 → 选 B

核心法律规则

严格产品责任（strict products liability）要先看到三个关键点：被告是商业销售者（commercial seller），产品在离开控制时就有缺陷，且缺陷造成了人身伤害或财产损害（physical harm）。

如果原告要的只是纯经济损失（purely economic loss），比如坏掉产品本身的损失、停业损失、少赚的钱，考试上通常不能靠严格责任拿赔偿。

这题里轮胎确实有制造缺陷，但车主只是因为轮胎打滑而少做了两单生意；这不是“身体受伤”或“别的财物被毁”，所以严格责任不救这个损失。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts: Prods. Liab. § 21 — 直接锁定：严格产品责任不赔纯经济损失。

思维导图

先问：原告主张的是不是严格产品责任？
是看产品有无缺陷、是否在制造商控制外就已存在缺陷。
本题轮胎确有制造缺陷，但关键不是“有没有缺陷”，而是“赔什么损失”。
再问：损害是 physical harm 还是纯经济损失？
本题只丢了两场 landscaping appointments 的收入，属于纯经济损失。
卡死点：effectively unreviewable 不是本题语言；本题卡的是“没有身体伤害/财产损害”。
结论：严格责任能不能救？
不能因为损失类型不对，制造商最佳抗辩就是：不承担纯经济损失。
答案选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：轮胎坏了、工作也耽误了，看起来很惨，应该能告制造商。

但考试真正问的是：严格责任能不能处理纯经济损失（purely economic loss），不是这批轮胎到底值不值得同情。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以别被“轮胎有缺陷”带跑：缺陷存在不等于损害类型合格。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键伤害是miss two landscaping appointments，这只是收入损失；严格产品责任不赔这种纯经济损失，所以制造商最强抗辩就是 B。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把assumed the risk当成本题主规则了。

❌ 事实误判 | 断链条件偷换

✕ C: 误以为二手转卖就切断责任链，题干没给这个结论。

❌ 法律适用 | 默示担保错位

✕ D: 把Not brand new拿来谈免责声明，但本题不是担保诉讼。

这题建议用什么方法？

先定责任理论，再卡损害类型；只要没有人身伤害或财产损害，就先排除严格责任。

考场速记

记住一句：严格产品责任（strict products liability）先看缺陷，再看有没有physical harm；只有“坏了但没伤人、没毁别的财物”的，通常就是纯经济损失，不能靠它赢。

速记：physical harm in, economic loss out。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A movie theater brought an action against a manufacturer and a retailer based solely on strict products liability for damages suffered when the theater's $20,000 movie projector caught on fire. While the fire destroyed the projector, it caused no property damage to its surroundings and no bodily harm because the projectionist put out the fire before it could spread. The movie theater sought economic damages based on the cost of the projector, as well as lost profits for the week the theater was closed until a replacement projector could be obtained.
At trial, the court ruled that because the projector had been destroyed, the theater was entitled to an inference that it was defective, which the defendants were free to rebut. The manufacturer presented evidence clearly showing that the only damage sustained by the theater was the destruction of the projector. The manufacturer and the retailer then filed a joint motion for a directed verdict.
Should the court grant the motion?

choices.A: No as to both defendants, because the court must infer that the projector was defective.
choices.B: No as to both defendants, because the theater is entitled to recover economic losses.
choices.C: Yes as to both defendants, because the theater suffered purely economic losses.
choices.D: Yes as to the retailer only, because the retailer was not involved in the manufacture of the projector.

questions.explanation:
Directed verdict
(strict products liability)

π presents legally sufficient evidence that:

I inferred if harm:
• usually results from defect and
• not solely due to other causes
Δ was commercial seller
  • Manufacturer
  • Distributor
  • Retailer
+
Product defective at time
left Δ's control
  • Manufacturing defect
  • Design defect
  • Inadequate warning
+
Defect caused π physical harm
  • Bodily harm
  • Property damage
↓
Yes
Reasonable jury could find for Δ
Yes
↓
Send case to jury
No
Directed verdict for π

π = plaintiff, Δ = defendant

A motion for a directed verdict should be granted if no reasonable jury could find in the nonmovant's favor. For example, a defendant's motion should be granted if there is insufficient evidence to support any element of the plaintiff's claim. A strict products liability claim requires proof of the following elements:

  • The defendant(s) were commercial sellers (eg, manufacturer, retailer - as seen here).
  • The product was defective at the time it left the defendant's control.
  • The defect caused the plaintiff's physical harm (ie, bodily harm or property damage).

As a result, claims for purely economic loss are not allowed. In products liability cases, purely economic loss includes any harm to the defective product itself as well as consequential damages arising therefrom (eg, lost profits).

Here, the movie theater is only seeking to recover damages based on the cost of the defective projector and lost profits - both of which are purely economic losses. Therefore, the theater has not suffered adequate damages to recover under its strict products liability claim, and the motion for a directed verdict should be granted as to both defendants.

(Choice A) Although the theater was entitled to an inference that the projector was defective, the theater cannot recover for its purely economic losses. And since the theater failed to allege property damage or personal injury, the court should grant the defendants' motion for a directed verdict.

(Choice B) The movie theater may have been entitled to recover economic losses that stemmed from bodily harm or damage to property other than the defective product itself (not seen here).

(Choice C) Commercial sellers are subject to strict liability for a defective product even if they were not responsible for the defect in any way. Accordingly, the retailer cannot escape liability on the basis that it was not involved in the manufacture of the projector.

(Choice D) Commercial sellers are subject to strict liability for a defective product even if they were not responsible for the defect in any way. Accordingly, the retailer cannot escape liability on the basis that it was not involved in the manufacture of the projector.

📌 Educational Objective

Strict products liability claims require proof of physical harm (ie, bodily harm or property damage). Claims for purely economic loss, including harm to the defective product itself and consequential damages arising therefrom, are not allowed.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Prods. Liab. § 21 (Am. Law Inst. 1998) (economic loss).
questions.zh-question:
题目：侵权法（Torts）——严格责任（Strict Liability）与产品责任（Products Liability）

一家电影院就严格产品责任（strict products liability）向一名制造商和一名零售商提起诉讼，要求赔偿其价值 20,000 美元的电影放映机起火所造成的损失。火灾虽然烧毁了放映机，但并未对周围财产造成任何损害，也未造成人身伤害，因为放映员在火势蔓延前将火扑灭。电影院请求赔偿经济损失，包括放映机的成本，以及在更换放映机到位前影院停业一周所损失的利润。

在审理中，法院裁定：由于放映机已被毁坏，电影院有权推定该放映机存在缺陷（defective），而被告可以对此推定提出反驳。制造商提出证据，明确表明电影院遭受的唯一损失就是放映机被毁。随后，制造商和零售商共同提出了定向裁决动议（motion for a directed verdict）。

法院是否应当准许该动议？

zh-choices.A: 否，对两名被告都不应准许，因为法院必须推定该放映机存在缺陷。
zh-choices.B: 否，对两名被告都不应准许，因为电影院有权获得经济损失赔偿。
zh-choices.C: 是，对两名被告都应准许，因为电影院遭受的只是纯粹的经济损失（purely economic losses）。
zh-choices.D: 是，仅对零售商应准许，因为零售商并未参与该放映机的制造。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Strict Liability and Products Liability - Strict products liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：严格产品责任里，只有人身伤害或财产损失（property damage）才能赔；如果只掉进了纯经济损失（pure economic loss），就不能靠这个理论拿赔偿。

三秒认题路径：

严格产品责任 → 只伤机器 → 没伤外物 → 只有经济损失 → 直接判输

核心法律规则

严格产品责任（strict products liability）要先看三件事：被告是商业卖家（commercial seller），产品在离开其控制时就有缺陷，且缺陷造成了原告的物理伤害（physical harm）。考场意思：不是“产品坏了”就够了，得有人身伤害或别的财产被打坏。

如果受损的只有缺陷产品本身，再加上停业损失、利润损失这类后果，属于纯经济损失（pure economic loss），不能用严格产品责任去收。考场意思：你能不能换一个理论主张，但这道题已经限定“只靠严格产品责任”，所以直接卡死。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts: Products Liability § 21 的思路就是：产品本身坏掉和连带停业损失，通常不算本题里能赔的损害。

思维导图

先问：原告有没有拿到严格产品责任能要的损害？
第1关：被告是商业卖家（commercial seller）？
这题里有：制造商 + 零售商，都进门。
第2关：产品离开控制时就有缺陷？
法院已给“可推定有缺陷”的线索，但这不是最后输赢点。
第3关：缺陷造成的是物理伤害（physical harm）吗？
不是。只烧毁投影机本身 + 停业利润，属于pure economic loss。
结论：第三关没过，原告证据不够 → 应对两名被告都作出 directed verdict：选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然火把投影机都烧没了，那原告总该能赢吧。

但考试真正问的是：严格产品责任能不能赔产品本身损坏和停业利润，不是问产品有没有真的坏。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这里最容易把“缺陷存在”误当成“可赔损害成立”；其实这题卡在损害类型，不卡在缺陷推定。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干明确只有投影机本身烧毁和停业利润，没有别的财产损失或人身伤害，所以是pure economic loss，严格产品责任下不能赔。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“可推定有缺陷”当成“当然能赢”。

❌ 事实误判 | 经济损失扩张误判

✕ B: 把lost profits误当可赔损害。

❌ 法律适用 | 零售商免责误判

✕ D: 以为零售商没参与制造就能脱身。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓损害类型，再看缺陷和被告身份；只要没有物理伤害，严格产品责任就先停。

考场速记

记住一句：产品坏了，不等于严格产品责任一定能赔；要先看有没有人身伤害或其他财产损失，只有机器自己坏掉和利润损失，通常就是pure economic loss。

reason.en: Shows recovery is limited to economic loss, which strict products liability does not cover.

reason.en: The court must grant the motion if no reasonable jury could find for the theater.
reason.zh: 若无合理陪审团可支持原告，法院应批准该动议。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A farmer owns a small farm with several head of cattle, which are kept in a fenced grazing area. One day the cattle were frightened by a thunderstorm, an occasional occurrence in the area. The cattle broke through the fence, entered onto a neighbor's property, and severely damaged the neighbor's crops. Under the law of the state, landowners are not required to erect fences to prevent the intrusion of livestock.
If the neighbor sues the farmer to recover for the damage done to his crops, will the neighbor prevail?

choices.A: No, because the thunderstorm was a force of nature.
choices.B: No, unless the fence was negligently maintained by the farmer.
choices.C: Yes, because the farmer's cattle caused the damage to the neighbor's crops.
choices.D: Yes, if the farmer's cattle had panicked during previous thunderstorms.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Imposition of strict liability
(liability imposed regardless of fault)
Abnormally dangerous activities
  • Uncommon activity in community that poses foreseeable & highly significant risk of physical harm
  • Risk cannot be minimized by reasonable care and
  • Physical harm caused by abnormal danger
Intrusion by livestock
  • Foreseeable intrusion of livestock onto land of another and
  • Intrusion causes physical harm typical of livestock (eg, consumption of grass)
Wild animals
  • Category of typically undomesticated animal likely to cause personal injury unless restrained (eg, poisonous snake) and
  • Physical harm caused by animal's abnormal danger
Abnormally dangerous animals
  • Animal with dangerous tendencies other animals in that category typically lack (eg, rabid dog)
  • Owner/possessor knows or should know of danger and
  • Physical harm results from that danger
Strict products liability
  • Harm caused by commercial supplier's defective product and
  • Defect existed when product left commercial supplier's control

Strict liability (liability without proof of fault) is imposed when livestock or other animals (not dogs or cats) enter another's land and cause bodily harm or property damage typical of livestock (eg, consumption of grass). But since the cause of the intrusion must be foreseeable, strict liability is not imposed when the intrusion is caused by an unforeseeable event or force—eg, stranger opens cattle gate, unpredictable tornado destroys fence.

Here, the farmer's cattle broke through his fence because they were frightened by a thunderstorm—an occasional (and therefore foreseeable) occurrence in the area. And since the cattle intruded onto the neighbor's land and damaged his crops, the farmer is strictly liable for that damage.

(Choice A) Because the thunderstorm was a foreseeable force of nature, it does not relieve the farmer of strict liability.

(Choice B) Although the farmer kept his cattle in a fenced area, he had no duty to erect a fence to prevent the cattle from escaping under state law. And since strict liability is imposed without proof of fault, the farmer's negligent maintenance of the fence is irrelevant.

(Choice D) While the intervening event that caused the intrusion must be foreseeable to impose strict liability, the effect of that event need not have been. Therefore, the farmer would be strictly liable even if his cattle had panicked during a previous thunderstorm.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant is strictly liable when his/her livestock foreseeably enter onto another's land and cause physical harm (ie, bodily harm or property damage) typical of livestock. However, a defendant is not strictly liable for a livestock intrusion caused by an unforeseeable act or force—eg, an unprecedented earthquake.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 21 (Am. Law Inst. 2010) (strict liability for livestock intrusion).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 34 reporter's note to cmt. d (Am. Law Inst. 2010) (foreseeable force of nature does not negate strict liability).
questions.zh-question:
一位农场主拥有一个小型农场，饲养着几头牛，这些牛被圈养在一个有围栏的牧区里。一天，牛群受到了一场雷暴的惊吓，雷暴在该地区偶尔会发生。牛群冲破了围栏，进入了邻居的地产，并严重损坏了邻居的庄稼。根据该州的法律，土地所有者没有被要求建立围栏以防止牲畜的侵入。

如果邻居起诉该农场主，要求赔偿其庄稼所受的损害，邻居会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为雷暴是自然之力。
zh-choices.B: 不会，除非该农场主对围栏的维护存在过失。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为农场主的牛对邻居的庄稼造成了损害。
zh-choices.D: 会，如果该农场主的牛在之前的雷暴中曾受过惊吓。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Strict Liability and Products Liability - Animals

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：家畜越界造成农作物损失时，是否适用严格责任（strict liability），以及可预见的自然事件会不会切断责任。

三秒认题路径：

家畜越界 → 农作物受损 → 看严格责任 → 先看可预见性 → 不能免责

核心法律规则

只抓这条规则

严格责任（strict liability）不看过错，只看损害是不是由这类危险自己带出来的。对牲畜侵入（intrusion by livestock），只要牲畜可预见地进入他人土地并造成像农作物损坏这类典型后果，主人就要赔。

可预见的自然力量（foreseeable force of nature）不会自动免除责任；只有那种真正打断因果链的不可预见事件，才可能让严格责任停住。

核心判例：Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liability for Physical and Emotional Harm § 21 的逻辑是：牲畜可预见越界并致损，就进严格责任；可预见雷暴不把责任切掉。

思维导图

先问：这是终局判决吗？
不是。 这题不是在考能不能立刻上诉，而是在考牲畜侵入后谁承担损失。
再看：牲畜为何冲出围栏？
可预见。 雷暴（thunderstorm）在该地区是偶发且可预见的，不是切断责任的怪事。
关键门槛：进入他人土地并造成典型损害？
是。 牲畜进入邻地并损坏庄稼，正是家畜侵入的典型结果。
卡死点：不用找过错；不需要先证明围栏维护疏忽。
结论：是否严格责任？
是。 所以邻居能赢，选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：thunderstorm 既然是自然事件，那农夫就不该负责。

但考试真正问的是：这场风暴是不是不可预见到足以打断严格责任；本题里它只是当地偶发天气，所以不能免责。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的关键事实是牲畜进入邻地并毁坏庄稼，这正是家畜侵入的典型损害，所以直接触发严格责任。

❌ 法律适用 | 自然力量误判

✕ A: 把force of nature当成自动免责，但本题的风暴是可预见的。

❌ 概念混淆 | 过错要件误判

✕ B: 误把严格责任当成过失责任，才会去盯着围栏是否维护疏忽。

❌ 事实误判 | 既往惊吓误判

✕ D: 以为以前也受惊就能改变结论，但题目要看这次越界是否可预见。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定牲畜侵入，再问事件是否不可预见；只要是可预见越界，直接走严格责任。

考场速记

记住一句：牲畜可预见越界 + 典型农损 = 严格责任；只有真正不可预见的外力，才可能切断责任。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 这类中间上诉口诀只在程序题里用，本题别跑偏；动物题就盯可预见性和典型损害。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A chef purchased a new food processor from a kitchen appliance manufacturer. The chef used the food processor for years and was always satisfied with its performance. He sold the food processor to an artist who specialized in unconventional materials. The first day the artist had the food processor, she used it to shred small pieces of scrap metal. When she turned on the food processor, the blade quickly rattled free, struck the side of the processing chamber, and shattered the chamber wall. Because the artist was holding the side of the appliance when it failed, a sharp edge of the broken chamber wall cut her palm, damaging the ligaments in her hand.
In a jurisdiction that applies the risk-utility test to determine whether a design defect exists, the artist has brought a strict products liability claim against the manufacturer. At trial, she has established that when the food processor was built, an economically feasible alternative material was available that could have been used to make the processing chamber such that it would not have shattered in the way that injured her hand.
Of the following, which is the manufacturer's strongest defense against the artist's strict products liability claim?

choices.A: The chef's prolonged use of the food processor was a superseding cause that cuts off the manufacturer's liability.
choices.B: The chef used the food processor for years with no sign that it was defective.
choices.C: The artist did not buy the food processor from a retail seller.
choices.D: The artist put the food processor to an improper and unforeseeable use.

questions.explanation:
Foreseeable use v. misuse

When a commercial supplier's defective product causes harm to the plaintiff, the supplier is subject to strict products liability absent some defense. One defense that negates a commercial supplier's strict liability is the plaintiff's misuse of the product (i.e., using the product in an unintended and unforeseeable manner).

Here, the manufacturer's food processor injured the artist when the chamber wall broke and cut her palm. At trial, the artist demonstrated that the design of the food processor was defective. But the manufacturer's liability was negated because the artist was missing the food processor by shredding small pieces of scrap metal instead of food. Therefore, the manufacturer's strongest defense against the artist's strict products liability claim is that the artist put the food processor to an improper and unforeseeable use.

(Choice A) The original manufacturer's liability may be cut off by a superseding cause if the product substantially changes after the manufacturer distributes the product and before it reaches the consumer. However, the chef's prolonged use of the food processor does not constitute a substantial change.

(Choice B) Although the chef used the food processor for years with no sign that it was defective, this is not a defense in a strict products liability claim.

(Choice C) Casual sellers (i.e., sellers not in the business of selling products) are not liable under a strict products liability theory (e.g., the chef). But the artist sued the manufacturer--not the chef. As a commercial seller, the manufacturer could be held liable unless the artist's misuse of the food processor negates strict liability.

📌 Educational Objective

A plaintiff cannot recover in a strict products liability action if the plaintiff was using the product in an unintended and unforeseeable way when the injury occurred.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Prods. Liab. § 15 (Am. Law Inst. 1998) (defining misuse of a product).

在一个适用 risk-utility test（风险效用测试）来判断是否存在 design defect（设计缺陷）的法域中，这名艺术家对制造商提起了 strict products liability（严格产品责任）诉讼。在审理中，她已经证明：在该 food processor 制造时，市场上存在一种经济上可行的替代材料，可以用来制造加工腔，从而使其不会以这种方式破裂并伤害她的手。

以下哪一项是制造商对艺术家的 strict products liability 诉讼最强有力的抗辩？

zh-choices.A: 厨师长期使用这台 food processor 构成了 superseding cause（介入原因/中断因果关系的原因），切断了制造商的责任。
zh-choices.B: 厨师使用这台 food processor 多年，而没有任何迹象表明它存在缺陷。
zh-choices.C: 艺术家并不是从零售卖家处购买这台 food processor 的。
zh-choices.D: 艺术家将这台 food processor 用于不当且不可预见的用途。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Strict Liability and Products Liability - Strict Liability and Products Liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：产品责任里，原告如果把产品拿去做了不当且不可预见的用途（misuse），制造商可以用这个抗辩挡掉严格责任。

三秒认题路径：

严格责任 → 设计缺陷 → 不当用途 → 不可预见 → 选 D

核心法律规则

在严格产品责任（strict products liability）里，商业卖方通常要为缺陷产品致害负责，前提是产品被拿来做的是预期且可预见的用途（intended and foreseeable use）。如果原告把产品拿去做不当且不可预见的用途（misuse），这会切断制造商的责任链。考场意思：不是问机器“坏没坏”，而是问这次受伤是不是因为原告把它当错了东西用。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts: Prods. Liab. § 15 — 说明产品 misuse 会否定严格责任；本题就卡在“把食物处理器拿去碎金属”这个点。

思维导图

先看：这是终局判决吗？
是能上诉；但本题不是这个路口。
否继续看有没有法定中间上诉。
再看附带命令原则（collateral-order doctrine）三要件。
1. 重要问题？可能有。
2. 与案件实体分离？可能有。
3. 能否在终局后有效救济？通常能。
看到律师特权披露令 → 联想 Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter → 结论：通常不能立刻上诉。
本题落点：商事制造商的责任不是被“坏了”卡死，而是被“misuse”卡死。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：机器先前被人长期正常使用，所以厂家应当继续负责。

但考试真正问的是：艺术家把食品处理器拿去碎scrap metal，这已经是不当且不可预见的用途（misuse）。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的关键事实是艺术家第一天就把机器拿去碎scrap metal，这不是处理食物的正常使用，所以制造商最强抗辩就是misuse。

❌ 法律适用 | 介入原因误判

✕ A: 前任买主长期使用不等于切断责任。

❌ 概念混淆 | 使用史误判

✕ B: “以前没坏过”不是严格责任的抗辩。

❌ 事实误判 | 卖家身份偷换

✕ C: 这题告的是制造商，不是把机器转卖的 chef。

这题建议用什么方法？

先盯住“用了什么用途”再判责任，不要被产品曾经正常工作带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：strict liability 不怕“用了很久”，最怕“拿去乱用”。看到“食品设备拿去碎金属”这种组合，优先想到misuse，直接排掉制造商责任。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A pop star hired a seamstress to sew several leather outfits for his upcoming musical tour. The seamstress needed a new sewing machine for the project, so she went to a retail store that specialized in sewing machines. While she was browsing, a sales associate approached her. Although the sales associate did not know the particular purpose for which the seamstress was buying a sewing machine, he told her to buy a specific model, stating, "This model is the best one on the market!" Relying upon his opinion, the seamstress purchased the sewing machine. However, when the seamstress tried to sew the pieces of the leather outfits together, the sewing machine could not sew through the thick leather. As a result, the seamstress was unable to make the leather outfits in time for the pop star's musical tour, and she lost thousands of dollars in profit.
The seamstress brought a products liability action against the retail store, alleging a breach of the implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose.
For whom will the court likely decide?

choices.A: The retail store, because the sales associate did not know the particular purpose for which the sewing machine was being purchased.
choices.B: The retail store, because the seamstress cannot recover for purely economic loss.
choices.C: The seamstress, because she relied on the sales associate's opinion when purchasing the sewing machine.
choices.D: The seamstress, because the sewing machine was not generally acceptable or reasonably fit for the purpose for which it had been sold.

questions.explanation:
Warranties for products liability actions
Implied Merchantability Product is generally acceptable & reasonably fit for its ordinary purpose—if seller is merchant
Fitness for particular purpose Product is fit for particular purpose—if seller has reason to know purchaser is relying on seller's skill or judgment to furnish suitable product
Express Any affirmation of fact or promise made by seller regarding product that is part of basis of bargain

A buyer may bring a products liability action against a seller of goods for breach of certain warranties, including the implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose. This implied warranty guarantees that a product is fit for a particular purpose, but only if:

  • the seller knows the particular purpose for which the product is being purchased and
  • the buyer relies on the seller's judgment or skill in selecting a product suitable for that purpose.

The warranty is breached if a product fails to live up to the standards imposed by this warranty, and the buyer need not prove that the seller was at fault. The buyer can then recover damages for personal injury or property damage, as well as for purely economic loss (Choice B).

Here, the sales associate did not know the particular purpose for which the sewing machine was being purchased (ie, to sew leather), so there was no implied warranty that the sewing machine was fit for that purpose. This is true even though the seamstress relied on the sales associate's opinion when purchasing the sewing machine (Choice C). Therefore, the sewing machine's inability to sew through leather was not a breach of this warranty, and the court will likely decide for the retail store.

(Choice B) The implied warranty of merchantability guarantees that a product is acceptable and reasonably fit for the ordinary purpose for which it is being sold—eg, a sewing machine can sew through ordinary fabrics. But here, the seamstress's claim is based solely on the implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose.

📌 Educational Objective

The implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose applies when (1) the seller knows the particular purpose for which the product is being purchased and (2) the buyer relies on the seller's judgment or skill in selecting a product suitable for that purpose. Breach of this warranty can give rise to a products liability claim.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-315 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose).

一位流行歌手聘请了一位女裁缝，为他即将到来的音乐巡演缝制几套皮革服装。这位女裁缝为这个项目需要一台新的缝纫机，于是她去了一家专营缝纫机的零售店。当她浏览商品时，一名销售助理走近了她。尽管销售助理不知道女裁缝购买缝纫机的特定目的，但他告诉她购买一个特定型号，并声称：“这个型号是市面上最好的！”女裁缝信赖他的意见，购买了这台缝纫机。然而，当女裁缝试图将皮革服装的各部分缝合在一起时，这台缝纫机无法缝透厚皮革。结果，女裁缝未能及时为这位流行歌手的音乐巡演制作好皮革服装，并损失了数千美元的利润。

女裁缝对该零售店提起了产品责任诉讼，指控其违反了特定目的适用性的默示担保。

法院可能会做出对谁有利的判决？

zh-choices.A: 零售店，因为销售助理不知道该缝纫机被购买的特定目的。
zh-choices.B: 零售店，因为女裁缝不能就纯粹的经济损失获得赔偿。
zh-choices.C: 女裁缝，因为她在购买缝纫机时信赖了销售助理的意见。
zh-choices.D: 女裁缝，因为该缝纫机并非普遍可接受，也未能合理地适用于其销售目的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Strict Liability and Products Liability - Warranties

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：适合特定用途的默示保证（implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose）是否成立，关键看卖方是否知道买方的“特定用途”。

三秒认题路径：

知道特定用途？ → 依赖卖方判断？ → 不是普通用途？ → 保证是否成立 → 选卖方赢

核心法律规则

适合特定用途的默示保证（implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose）只在两件事同时满足时才成立：卖方知道买方要拿产品做什么，买方还确实依赖卖方的技能或判断来挑合适商品。

考场意思：卖方不知道“你是要缝皮革”，就不会因为产品最后缝不动皮革而自动背上这个保证责任。

适销性默示保证（implied warranty of merchantability）问的是普通用途能不能用，不是这次的特殊任务能不能完成，所以这题不能把它拿来代替。

核心判例： U.C.C. § 2-315（规则来源）——卖方知道特定用途且买方依赖其判断时，才会成立“适合特定用途”的默示保证。

思维导图

先问：卖方是否知道买方的特定用途？
NO 没有“知道要缝皮革” → 第三题眼：保证不成立 → 选 A
YES 再问：买方是否依赖卖方判断选货？
YES 才进入 适合特定用途的默示保证（implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose）
NO 没有依赖 → 仍然不成立
本题事实：销售员只说“最好”，但不知道用途 → 直接卡死在第一关。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：买方确实听了销售员的话，而且机器最后坏在“不能缝皮革”，好像应该由店里负责。

但考试真正问的是：卖方当时知不知道这台机器是要拿去做“缝皮革”这种特定用途。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能成立这个保证」，而不是「机器用起来让人多失望」。

所以，单靠“best one on the market”这种夸奖，不会自动变成 适合特定用途的默示保证（implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose）。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的sales associate did not know the particular purpose正好缺了成立要件，所以这个默示保证没生出来，店家赢。

❌ 事实误判 | 经济损失偷换

✕ B: 抓着 purely economic loss 乱套，题目考的是保证是否成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 依赖误当知道

✕ C: 只看到依赖，就把“卖方知道用途”这一关漏掉了。

❌ 法律适用 | 适销性错位

✕ D: 把 merchantable 当成本题规则，偷换成普通用途标准。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“卖方是否知道特定用途”，再看买方依赖；缺一项，保证就直接断掉。

考场速记

记住一句：特定用途要默示保证，先看卖方知不知道，再看买方有没有靠他挑。

对比口诀：普通用途看 merchantability，特殊任务看 fitness for a particular purpose。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A bartender was removing the restraining wire from a bottle of champagne produced and bottled by a wine company when the plastic stopper suddenly shot out of the bottle. The stopper struck and injured the bartender's eye. The bartender had opened other bottles of champagne, and occasionally the stoppers had shot out with great force, but he had not been injured.
The bartender brought an action against the wine company, and the jury found that the bottle that caused his injury was defective and unreasonably dangerous because its label did not warn that the stopper might suddenly shoot out during opening. The state has merged contributory negligence and unreasonable assumption of risk into a pure comparative-fault system that is applied in strict products liability actions.
Will the bartender recover a judgment in his favor?

choices.A: No, if a reasonable bartender would have realized that a stopper could eject from the bottle and hit his eye.
choices.B: No, if the jury finds that even with a legally sufficient warning, the bartender would have opened the bottle the same way he had in the past.
choices.C: Yes, with damages reduced by the percentage of any contributory fault on the bartender's part.
choices.D: Yes, with no reduction in damages, because foreseeable lack of caution is the reason for requiring a warning.

questions.explanation:
Strict products liability for inadequate warnings
Is product defective?
  • Product poses foreseeable and unobvious risk of harm to users
  • Adequate warnings could reduce that risk
No→Not liable
↓
Did product cause harm?
  • Plaintiff suffers physical harm
  • Harm would not have occurred had adequate warnings been provided
No→Not liable
↓
Liable

Under products liability law, commercial suppliers are required to provide adequate warnings (or instructions) when:

• their product poses a foreseeable and unobvious risk of physical harm and

• reasonable warnings could reduce that risk.

Failure to provide adequate warnings renders a product defective and subjects a commercial supplier to strict liability when that defect causes the plaintiff’s harm. To prove that the defect caused his/her harm, the plaintiff must show that the harm would not have occurred had a legally sufficient warning been provided.

The bar tender was injured by a champagne bottle stopper. The jury found that the bottle was defective due to its lack of warning about the stopper. But if the jury also finds that a legally sufficient warning would not have prevented the bartender's injury—for example, that even with a warning, the bartender would have opened the bottle the same way he had in the past—then the bottle's absent warning did not cause his injury and he will not prevail.

(Choice A) If a reasonable bartender would have realized the stopper's risk of harm, the bartender may have contributed to his harm by failing to protect himself against that risk (contributory negligence). However, the bartender's contributory negligence would merely reduce—not bar—his recovery in this pure comparative-fault jurisdiction.

(Choice B) If the bartender could obtain a judgment in his favor, his recovery would be reduced by his percentage of fault in this pure comparative-fault system—for example, bartender 60% at fault would still recover 40% of his damages. But if the jury finds that a sufficient warning would not have prevented his injury (e.g., because he would have ignored the warning), then none of his harm was caused by the absent warning and he will recover nothing.

(Choice C) The fact that the user’s lack of caution may have been foreseeable would support the jury's finding that the bottle was defective. But to recover, the bartender must also prove that a legally sufficient warning would have prevented his injury.

(Choice D) No, if the fact that the user’s lack of caution may have been foreseeable would support the jury's finding that the bottle was defective. But to recover, the bartender must also prove that a legally sufficient warning would have prevented his injury.

📌 Educational Objective

A commercial supplier is strictly liable for harm caused by a defective product that lacks adequate warnings if legally sufficient warnings would have prevented the plaintiff's harm.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Prod. Liab. § 1, 2(c) cmt. i (Am. L. Inst. 1998) (strict products liability for inadequate warnings or instructions).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 26 cmt. g (Am. L. Inst. 2010) (harm caused by inadequate warnings).
questions.zh-question:
主题：侵权法（Torts）— 严格责任（Strict Liability）与产品责任（Products Liability）

题目：
一家酒吧调酒师正在从一家葡萄酒公司生产并装瓶的香槟酒瓶上拆除固定钢丝（restraining wire）时，瓶中的塑料瓶塞突然从瓶内弹出。瓶塞击中并伤害了调酒师的眼睛。该调酒师以前曾打开过其他香槟瓶，而且有时瓶塞也会猛烈弹出，但他从未受伤。

调酒师对该葡萄酒公司提起诉讼，陪审团认定，导致其受伤的那瓶酒存在缺陷（defective）且具有不合理危险（unreasonably dangerous），因为其标签未警告瓶塞在开启时可能会突然弹出。该州已将 contributory negligence 和 unreasonable assumption of risk 合并为 pure comparative-fault 体系，并将其适用于严格产品责任（strict products liability）案件。

调酒师能否获得对其有利的判决？

zh-choices.A: 不能，如果一个合理的调酒师会意识到瓶塞可能会从瓶中弹出并击中他的眼睛。
zh-choices.B: 不能，如果陪审团认定，即使有法律上充分的警告，调酒师也会像过去一样以同样方式开启该瓶。
zh-choices.C: 可以，但损害赔偿应按调酒师自身任何 contributory fault 的比例减少。
zh-choices.D: 可以，且不减少赔偿，因为可预见的缺乏谨慎正是要求警告的原因。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Strict Liability and Products Liability - Products liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：产品缺少警告时，原告不只要证明产品有风险，还要证明adequate warning真的能避免这次受伤。

三秒认题路径：

缺警告 → 看因果 → 会阻止伤害吗 → 不会就不赔 → 选 B

核心法律规则

只抓这条就够了

严格产品责任（strict products liability）里，商家要给adequate warnings（充分警告），前提是产品对使用者存在可预见、但不明显的伤害风险，而且警告能降低这个风险。

但光有缺警告还不够；原告还要证明causation，也就是如果当时给了合法充分的警告，这次伤害就不会发生。

所以这题的关键不是“酒瓶会不会弹出”，而是“这张警告牌能不能真的改变 bartender 的动作”。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts: Products Liability 的思路锁定本题：没有足够警告时，仍要看缺陷是否真的造成这次损害。

思维导图

产品缺少警告，先问：这次伤害是“警告缺失”造成的吗？
先看缺陷：酒瓶对使用者有不明显但可预见的弹出风险，且警告本可降低风险。
再问：如果有合法充分的警告，bartender 还会不会照样这么开？
YES 还会照样开 → 警告没有改变结果，因果链断了 → 不赔
NO 会因此改变操作 → 伤害由缺警告造成 → 可赔
纯比较过失只是在“已经可赔”时减额，不会把“没因果”的案子救活。
结论：本题落点是“合法充分的警告是否会避免受伤”，答案选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他以前就见过瓶塞猛弹，说明自己也有点不小心，所以应该按过失比例减赔。

但考试真正问的是：司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这题先看缺警告是否真的造成伤害；只有先过了因果这一关，才轮到比较过失减额。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干已经说瓶子缺警告而有缺陷，但如果 bartender 就算收到合法充分警告也还是照旧开瓶，那缺警告就没有造成这次眼伤，不能判他赢。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“他本可注意风险”当成直接挡赔，但这只会碰到comparative fault。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间上诉理由误判

✕ C: 以为纯比较过失一定只是按比例减赔，但前提是伤害先得真由缺警告造成。

❌ 事实误判 | 题干条件偷换

✕ D: 把“可预见”直接等同于“必然可赔”，但这题还差would have prevented这一步。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“缺警告是否真的致害”，再看比较过失是否只是减额。

考场速记

记住一句：缺警告（failure to warn）不自动等于赔，原告还得证明“如果警告到位，这次伤就不会发生”。

遇到strict products liability，先问因果；先能救回伤害，才谈比例减责。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A hot-air balloon touring company operated near a golf course. The company's property was separated from the golf course by a fence on which the company had posted signs warning people not to enter the property because of the dangers of balloons landing.
A golfer on the golf course hit an errant shot onto the company's property, ignored the warning signs, and jumped over the fence to retrieve her golf ball. At about the same time, one of the company's balloons experienced mechanical problems and had to make an emergency landing to avoid crashing. The balloon, which was out of control when it landed, struck the golfer and injured her.
The jurisdiction has decided that hot-air ballooning is an abnormally dangerous activity.
In an action by the golfer against the company, does the company have any affirmative defenses?

choices.A: No, because the balloon was out of control when it struck the golfer.
choices.B: No, because the company was engaged in an abnormally dangerous activity.
choices.C: Yes, because the balloon landed to avoid crashing.
choices.D: Yes, because the golfer assumed the risk by coming onto the company's property.

questions.zh-question:
一家热气球旅游公司在高尔夫球场附近运营。该公司的地产与高尔夫球场之间由一道栅栏隔开，公司在栅栏上张贴了警示牌，警告人们因热气球着陆的危险，请勿进入该地产。

高尔夫球场上的一名高尔夫球手打出一个偏离的球，球落入了该公司的地产。她无视警示牌，翻过栅栏去捡球。大约在同一时间，该公司的一个热气球出现机械故障，为避免坠毁而不得不紧急着陆。热气球在着陆时失控，撞伤了该高尔夫球手。

该司法管辖区已裁定，热气球活动属于异常危险活动。

在高尔夫球手对该公司提起的诉讼中，该公司是否有任何积极抗辩事由？

zh-choices.A: 没有，因为热气球撞击高尔夫球手时已经失控。
zh-choices.B: 没有，因为该公司从事的是异常危险活动。
zh-choices.C: 有，因为热气球是为了避免坠毁而着陆的。
zh-choices.D: 有，因为高尔夫球手进入公司地产时，自担了风险。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Strict Liability and Products Liability - Defenses to strict liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：严格责任（strict liability）下，原告是否因为知道危险还自愿进去而构成风险承担（assumption of the risk）抗辩。

三秒认题路径：

严格责任 → 抗辩 → 知风险 → 自愿进 → 可免责

核心法律规则

异常危险活动（abnormally dangerous activity）导致的损害，通常适用严格责任（strict liability），意思是公司不靠“我已经很小心”来脱身。风险承担（assumption of the risk）是这里能用的抗辩，但前提是原告知道具体危险，还自愿接受这个危险。换成考场语言：只要原告是明知危险仍硬闯，后面被危险本身伤到，原告就很容易被这个抗辩挡回去。

核心判例：Restatement (Second) of Torts § 523 和 Restatement (Third) of Torts § 20 都把“明知并自愿接受风险”作为严格责任下的重要抗辩。

思维导图

题目先问：公司有没有可用的严格责任抗辩？
先看：原告是不是 知道危险（known risk）？
本题卡点：看见警告牌，说明她知道“球场外这块地有危险”。
再看：她是不是 自愿接受（voluntarily accept）？
本题卡点：她忽略警告，翻栏进入，属于自愿进去找球。
结论：两步都满足 → assumption of the risk 成立。
别被带跑：公司是不是很危险、球是不是失控，都不是这道题的主轴。
最终答案：公司有抗辩，选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：气球已经失控、还撞伤人，应该是公司不能靠任何理由免责。

但考试真正问的是：原告是不是明知危险还自愿冒进去，而不是公司当时有没有尽到合理注意。

司法考试看的是「法律上能不能用这个抗辩」，而不是「事故看起来多吓人」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里原告先看见警告牌，又翻越围栏进场，正好命中知道危险 + 自愿接受，所以公司能提风险承担（assumption of the risk）抗辩。

❌ 事实误判 | 失控细节误读

✕ A: 只盯着 out of control，却忽略了原告自己先知道风险。

❌ 法律适用 | 严责否定抗辩

✕ B: 把“严格责任”误听成“没有任何抗辩”，这是常见错法。

❌ 概念混淆 | 紧急着陆误判

✕ C: 气球为了避撞而降落，不会自动抹掉原告已经接受过的风险。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找严格责任能用的抗辩，再专门核对“知道危险 + 自愿接受”这两个点。

考场速记

记忆口诀：严格责任不怕多，先问原告知不知、又是不是自己跳进去。只要是know + voluntary，就优先想到assumption of the risk。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A manufacturer of baby gear designed a baby bouncer that allowed infants to jump up and down without parental assistance. The baby bouncer could be attached to a doorframe with a plastic clamp, which was connected to the baby seat via a spring and safety cord. The manufacturer designed the baby bouncer to safely withstand a maximum weight of 20 pounds, but if an infant exceeded that weight, there was a risk that the clamp could slip off of the doorframe and severely injure the infant. For a slightly higher cost, the manufacturer could have used a metal clamp that withstood a maximum weight of 40 pounds, but the manufacturer opted for the cheaper plastic clamp so that it could undercut its competitors. The manufacturer attached a warning label to the baby bouncer stating the weight limit and that if the limit was exceeded, the clamp could slip off the doorframe and injure an infant.
A mother purchased the manufacturer's baby bouncer for her nine-month-old infant who weighed 25 pounds. She read the warning label but chose to ignore the weight limit. After a few uses, the clamp slipped off the doorframe, and the infant suffered a concussion and broken leg from the fall.
The mother brought a strict products liability action against the manufacturer in a jurisdiction that applies traditional contributory negligence.
Who will likely prevail?

choices.A: The manufacturer, because it put a warning label on the baby bouncer regarding the weight limit.
choices.B: The manufacturer, because the mother chose to ignore the weight limit on the warning label.
choices.C: The mother, because the baby bouncer was defectively designed.
choices.D: The mother, because the weight limit was the result of a manufacturing defect.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Assumption of the risk
(defense to strict liability)
Traditional contributory negligence jurisdiction
  • Bars recovery when plaintiff voluntarily exposed him/herself to known risk
Pure comparative negligence jurisdiction*
  • Reduces recovery when plaintiff voluntarily exposed him/herself to known risk
  • Narrow exception: Bars recovery when plaintiff received benefit (eg, financial gain, employment) from his/her exposure to risk
* Default rule on MBE.

A plaintiff can prevail on a strict products liability claim if the defendant is a commercial supplier (eg, manufacturer) and its defective product caused the plaintiff harm. Under the risk-utility test, a product is defective by design when:

  • the design creates a foreseeable risk of harm and
  • that risk could have been mitigated by a reasonable alternative design (eg, a modification that reduces the risk for a reasonable cost).

However, in jurisdictions that apply the traditional rules of contributory negligence (as seen here), assumption of the risk completely bars a plaintiff's recovery for strict products liability when the plaintiff (1) knows of the product's risk of harm and (2) voluntarily uses the product despite that risk.

Here, the manufacturer's baby bouncer used a plastic clamp that could only withstand a maximum weight of 20 pounds. This created a foreseeable risk that the clamp could slip off and severely injure an infant. And this risk of harm could have been mitigated by using a metal clamp for a slightly higher cost. As a result, the bouncer was defectively designed (Choice C). But the mother assumed this risk because she read the warning label describing the risk (knowledge of risk) and chose to ignore it (voluntary use). Therefore, the manufacturer will likely prevail.

(Choice A) The fact that the manufacturer put a warning label on the baby bouncer regarding the weight limit is relevant to establishing that the mother knew about the risk of harm. But this fact alone does not absolve the manufacturer from strict products liability.

(Choice D) A product has a manufacturing defect if it deviates from the manufacturer's intended design (eg, due to incorrect assembly). Here, the baby bouncer was manufactured according to the manufacturer's design, so its weight limit was not the result of a manufacturing defect.

📌 Educational Objective

In a traditional contributory-negligence jurisdiction, the plaintiff's assumption of the risk—ie, voluntary use of a product despite its known risk of harm—is a complete bar to recovery for strict products liability.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Prod. Liab. § 1 (Am. Law Inst. 1998) (defining strict products liability).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts: § 523 (Am. Law Inst. 1977) (explaining strict liability and assumption of the risk).

主题：侵权法（Torts）——严格责任（Strict Liability）与产品责任（Products Liability）

问题：
一家婴儿用品制造商设计了一款婴儿跳跳椅（baby bouncer），可让婴儿在无需父母协助的情况下上下弹跳。该跳跳椅可以通过一个塑料夹子固定在门框上，并通过弹簧和安全绳与婴儿座椅相连。制造商将该婴儿跳跳椅设计为可安全承受最大 20 磅的重量，但如果婴儿超过该重量，夹子可能会从门框上滑脱，并对婴儿造成严重伤害。若多花一点成本，制造商本可以使用可承受最大 40 磅重量的金属夹子，但制造商为了压低价格、击败竞争对手，选择了更便宜的塑料夹子。制造商还在该婴儿跳跳椅上贴了警示标签，说明重量限制，并告知如果超过该限制，夹子可能会从门框上滑脱并伤害婴儿。

一位母亲为她 9 个月大的、体重 25 磅的婴儿购买了该制造商的婴儿跳跳椅。她读了警示标签，但仍选择无视重量限制。使用几次后，夹子从门框上滑脱，婴儿摔落，导致脑震荡和腿部骨折。

该母亲在一个适用传统 contributory negligence（共同过失）规则的司法辖区，对制造商提起 strict products liability（严格产品责任）诉讼。

谁更可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 制造商，因为其已就重量限制在婴儿跳跳椅上贴出了警示标签。
zh-choices.B: 制造商，因为母亲选择无视警示标签上的重量限制。
zh-choices.C: 母亲，因为该婴儿跳跳椅存在设计缺陷（defectively designed）。
zh-choices.D: 母亲，因为重量限制是制造缺陷（manufacturing defect）的结果。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Strict Liability and Products Liability - Strict liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：在传统过失相抵州里，消费者明知产品风险还继续用，是否会因 自甘风险（assumption of the risk） 直接挡掉严格产品责任赔偿。

三秒认题路径：

严格产品责任 → 已知风险 → 仍继续使用 → 自甘风险 → 不能赔

核心法律规则

严格产品责任（strict products liability）要先看产品有没有 设计缺陷（design defect）：设计让产品有可预见的伤害风险，而且存在合理可行的替代设计能在合理成本下降低风险。自甘风险（assumption of the risk） 的考场意思：原告知道这个危险，还主动继续用，传统 contributory negligence 州里会直接挡掉恢复。

这里最关键的不是“有没有贴警告”四个字，而是母亲已经读到警告，等于知道风险，却还是把 25 磅的婴儿放上去。控制判例是 Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 吗？不是，本题不是上诉题；它锁定的是风险已知后仍使用就会败诉这一条。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 523 与 Restatement (Third) of Torts: Prod. Liab. § 1 说明：知道风险还用，在传统过失相抵州里通常直接挡掉严格责任。

思维导图

先看：原告是不是知道产品会出事？
是 读过警告，知道 20 磅限重，也知道超重会滑落伤人。
再看 还要不要继续用？
继续用 = 自甘风险（assumption of the risk），传统 contributory negligence 州里直接卡死赔偿。
别被带偏 真缺陷是 设计缺陷（design defect），不是 制造缺陷（manufacturing defect）；贴警告也不洗白设计。
结论：先认出风险已知，再落到 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：厂商已经贴了警告，或者产品确实有设计问题，所以应该让母亲赢。

但考试真正问的是：母亲是不是明知风险还继续用。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这里的陷阱是把“产品有缺陷”当成终局结论，忘了传统 contributory negligence 下，自甘风险 可以直接把赔偿门关上。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

母亲读过警告，明知 25 磅仍继续使用，在传统过失相抵州里这就是 自甘风险，会挡掉她的严格责任请求。

❌ 概念混淆 | 警告等于免责

✕ A: 以为 warning label 一贴，厂商就自动脱身。

❌ 法律适用 | 设计缺陷硬套

✕ C: 抓到设计不安全就想当然让原告赢，忘了 assumption of the risk 已经截胡。

❌ 事实误判 | 制造缺陷偷换

✕ D: 把限重问题说成 manufacturing defect，题干根本没说装配跑偏。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓抗辩，再看缺陷类型；一旦读到警告后仍使用，先想自甘风险。

考场速记

记住一句话：知道危险还继续用，在传统过失相抵州里通常就是严格责任的“终止按钮”。

下次看到产品警告 + 明知仍用，先别急着想设计缺陷，先问：她是不是已经自甘风险了？

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A construction company was engaged in blasting operations to clear the way for a new road. The construction company had erected adequate barriers and posted adequate warning signs in the vicinity of the blasting. Although a hiker read and understood the signs, he entered the area to walk his dog. As a result of the blasting, the hiker was hit by a piece of rock and sustained head injuries. The jurisdiction follows the traditional common law rules governing the defenses of contributory negligence, assumption of risk, and last clear chance.
In an action by the hiker against the construction company to recover damages for his injuries, will the hiker prevail?

choices.A: No, because the construction company exercised reasonable care to protect the public from harm.
choices.B: No, because the hiker understood the signs and disregarded the warnings.
choices.C: Yes, because the hiker was harmed by the construction company's abnormally dangerous activity.
choices.D: Yes, unless the hiker failed to use reasonable care to protect himself from harm.

questions.explanation:
Assumption of the risk
(defense to strict liability)
Traditional contributory negligence jurisdiction • Bars recovery when plaintiff voluntarily exposed him/herself to known risk
Pure comparative negligence jurisdiction*
  • Reduces recovery when plaintiff voluntarily exposed him/herself to known risk
  • Narrow exception: Bars recovery when plaintiff received benefit (eg, financial gain, employment) from his/her exposure to risk

* Default rule on MBE.

Individuals who engage in abnormally dangerous activities are generally subject to strict liability. A strict liability claim requires proof that the plaintiff was harmed by the defendant's abnormally dangerous activity. But under the traditional common law rules, assumption of the risk is a complete defense to strict liability when the plaintiff voluntarily confronted a known risk of harm.

Here, the hiker was harmed by the construction company's abnormally dangerous activity—blasting (Choice C). However, the company erected barriers and warning signs near its blasting operations, which the hiker read and understood. And because the hiker voluntarily confronted that risk by disregarding the warnings and entering the dangerous area, he assumed the risk and cannot prevail in this common law jurisdiction.

(Choice A) Strict liability claims do not require proof of fault. Therefore, the construction company could be liable even though it exercised reasonable care by erecting adequate barriers and posting adequate warning signs.

(Choice D) Contributory negligence is not a defense to strict liability in common law jurisdictions. Therefore, the hiker's mere failure to use reasonable care for his own protection would not bar his recovery. Instead, the hiker's recovery is barred by his voluntary assumption of the risk.

📌 Educational Objective

Individuals who engage in abnormally dangerous activities are generally subject to strict liability for any resulting harm. But in traditional common law jurisdictions, assumption of the risk is a complete defense to strict liability if the plaintiff voluntarily confronted a known risk of harm.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 524 (Am. L. Inst. 1965) (explaining that contributory negligence is not a defense to strict liability unless the plaintiff's negligence amounts to assumption of the risk).

一家建筑公司正在进行爆破作业，为一条新路清障。该建筑公司在爆破区域附近设置了充分的屏障并张贴了充分的警示标志。尽管一名徒步者阅读并理解了这些标志，他还是进入该区域遛狗。因爆破作业，该徒步者被一块岩石击中，导致头部受伤。该司法管辖区遵循关于共同过失(contributory negligence)、风险自负(assumption of risk)和最后明显机会(last clear chance)抗辩的传统普通法规则。

在该徒步者对建筑公司提起的诉讼中，要求赔偿其所受伤害的损失，该徒步者能否胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该建筑公司已尽到合理注意义务以保护公众免受伤害。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该徒步者理解了标志并无视了警告。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该徒步者是因建筑公司的异常危险活动而受到伤害。
zh-choices.D: 会，除非该徒步者未能尽到合理注意义务以保护自己免受伤害。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Strict Liability and Products Liability - Strict liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：异常危险活动（abnormally dangerous activity）下，明知风险仍主动进入（assumption of the risk）是否能把严格责任挡掉。

三秒认题路径：

爆破 → 严格责任 → 知风险 → 还进去 → 不能赔

核心法律规则

一眼能用的规则

做异常危险活动（abnormally dangerous activity）的人，通常要对造成的损害承担严格责任（strict liability），不需要证明有过错。可是在普通法下，如果原告明知危险，还自愿面对已知风险（assumption of the risk），这就是完全抗辩，直接挡掉恢复赔偿。

这里的关键不是被告有没有尽到注意义务，而是原告有没有看懂警告后仍然硬闯危险区。contributory negligence（共同过失）通常不是严格责任的抗辩，所以“我自己不小心”这条路不够，真正卡死的是“我知道风险还去碰”。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 524 — 共同过失一般不挡严格责任，除非它已经高到等于assumption of the risk。

思维导图

题干先问：这是“严格责任 + 认风险”的题吗？
1. 被告在爆破，属于异常危险活动（abnormally dangerous activity） → 先想到 strict liability。
2. 原告看见并读懂警告牌、隔离栏 → 说明他不是不知道，而是明知风险。
3. 仍然走进危险区遛狗 → 这是自愿面对风险（assumption of the risk）。
卡死点：不是“被告做了什么”，而是“原告明知还进场” → 完全抗辩成立。
4. 结论：不能胜诉，选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：被告都做了爆破，而且原告真的受伤了，那是不是直接判严格责任赔钱？

但考试真正问的是：原告已经读懂警告，还自己走进危险区，这时先看assumption of the risk，不是先看被告有没有“已经很小心”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的read and understood the signs是致命事实：原告明知爆破风险仍进入危险区，构成assumption of the risk，所以不能胜诉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“被告很谨慎”当成免责理由，误把严格责任看成过错责任。

❌ 法律适用 | 结果直觉误判

✕ C: 只盯着abnormally dangerous，却漏掉原告自己把已知风险吃下去了。

❌ 事实误判 | 共同过失偷换

✕ D: 把“没尽到自我保护”当成挡箭牌，但这题真正挡赔的是知风险后仍自愿进入。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“原告是否明知仍进入”，再判断是不是严格责任里的assumption of the risk。

考场速记

记住一句：严格责任不怕“我很小心”，最怕“你明知风险还去碰”。看到爆破、化学、火灾这类异常危险活动，先问原告是不是已经看懂警告却仍主动靠近。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A mother purchased a used crib from a private estate auction. The estate sale was held by an auctioneer who often sold used personal property, including furniture, at auctions for estate sales. The crib was not assembled when the mother purchased it, so the mother put it together by herself when she got home. A few nights later, the crib collapsed while her baby was sleeping in it. The baby fractured her wrist in the fall. The mother sued the auctioneer under a strict products liability theory. At trial, it was established that the crib was defective as purchased from the auctioneer but that the mother was 20% at fault because she failed to screw in one slat of the crib properly.
Will the mother likely be able to collect damages from the auctioneer for her baby's injuries?

choices.A: No, because the auctioneer is not a seller subject to strict liability.
choices.B: No, because the mother was partially at fault for the crib collapsing.
choices.C: Yes, because the auctioneer sold a defective crib to the mother.
choices.D: Yes, because the auctioneer was in the business of selling furniture.

questions.explanation:
Products liability
Was plaintiff harmed by a product?
Yes
Who is the defendant?

Commercial seller

(eg, manufacturer, distributor, retailer)

Causes of action

  • Strict products liability (preferred)
  • Negligence
  • Misrepresentation
  • Intentional tort

Noncommercial seller

(eg, garage sale)

Causes of action

  • Negligence
  • Misrepresentation
  • Intentional tort

Service provider

(eg, doctor, dentist)

No products liability

Strict products liability applies to commercial suppliers—i.e., persons who regularly manufacture, distribute, or sell the type of defective product that caused the plaintiff harm. But it does not apply to casual sellers who are not in the regular business of selling the type of defective product that caused the plaintiff harm. Similarly, strict products liability generally does not apply to auctioneers.

(Choice C) Here, the mother sued the auctioneer under a strict products liability theory after the baby suffered a broken wrist when the used crib collapsed. At trial, it was established that the crib was defective as purchased from the auctioneer. Although the auctioneer sold the crib to the mother, the auctioneer is not a seller subject to strict liability. Therefore, the mother will likely not be able to collect damages from the auctioneer for her baby's injuries.

(Choice B) Most jurisdictions apply the comparative-negligence theory of recovery in negligence actions. Under this theory, the mother's recovery could be reduced because she was partially at fault, but it would not be barred.

(Choice D) Although the auctioneer was in the business of auctioning personal property, including furniture, the auctioneer is not considered a commercial supplier for strict liability purposes.

📌 Educational Objective

Strict products liability applies to commercial suppliers—i.e., persons who regularly manufacture, distribute, or sell the type of defective product that caused the plaintiff harm. But it does not apply to casual sellers or auctioneers.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Prods. Liab. §§ 1 cmt. c, 20 cmt. g (Am. L. Inst. 1998) (defining commercial supplier).
